title: Handing over a job without standing over anyone
target: Which duties in Supermarket Simulator can be handed over, and what each of them runs behind the scenes, so a worker is given a job rather than a hope.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)

steps.do: Hand over a duty that exists as a thing rather than asking for help in general.
steps.because: cashier duty is tied to items of its own, with a definition behind them (Cashier, CashierSO, CashierItem)

steps.do: Keep cashier duty and helper duty apart in your head.
steps.because: helper duty is tied to helper items rather than to the cashier (CustomerHelperItem, IceCreamHelperItem)

steps.do: Hand over the taking of an order, which is a task of its own.
steps.because: taking an order is a task that can be handed to a helper (StartCustomerHelperCheckoutOrder)

steps.do: Remember that serving at the till stays the checkout's own behaviour.
steps.because: starting a cashier checkout and finishing it belong to the checkout (StartCashierCheckout, FinishCheckout)

steps.do: Expect restocking to have machinery of its own rather than being generic work.
steps.because: restocking staff are run by a manager of their own and a restocker has a definition of its own (RestockerManager, RestockerSO)

steps.do: Check what state a restocker is in before deciding it is idle.
steps.because: a restocker works through states of its own, including one for restocking itself (RestockerState, RestockingState)

steps.do: Know that a clerk is animated by its own controller, so what you see is that job's animation rather than a generic worker.
steps.because: a clerk has an animation controller of its own (ClerkAnimationController)

steps.do: Remember the ice cream side has its own manager and its own generator settings.
steps.because: the ice cream stand has a manager of its own and keeps a set of generator settings (IceCreamManager, IceCreamGeneratorSettings)

commonMistakes: Expecting a helper to serve at the till when that belongs to the checkout.
Handing over restocking and then re-stacking the same shelves yourself.
Reading a restocker's paused state as it doing nothing.
Assuming every stand uses the same machinery as the tills.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
